to hunger for what is right; and to put others before our pride. these are not ideals reserved for a few exceptional people. they are a daily invitation to every christian. choosing love can be costly, especially when blame or indifference seems easier. yet we do not walk this path alone. the holy spirit helps us live in christ and reminds us that god is our father. all saints points us towards heaven, where we shall see god face to face. each loving choice offers a glimpse of that joynow. the saints’ invitation is ours too: let god’s love become visible through you. november novena for all the faithful departed begins on monday 2nd and end on tuesday 10th. there is daily mass in st. paul’s oratory at 10am (monday to friday) and in st. jos eph’s church at 7.30pm (monday to friday). saturday evening 6pm, sunday at 9.30am (grangecon) and 11am (st. jose ph’s, baltinglass). on saturday 7th at the 6pm mass, we have our annual mass for all who have died in the past 12 months with a special welcome to their families and friends. sick calls if you have anyone that’s sick or housebound and you would like a priest to visit please contact the parish ofoce. the irish catholic ireland’s biggest and best-selling religious newspaper. on sale in st. joseph’s church every weekend. please note if you take one please put money in the box. cost €3.80. eucharistic adoration st. paul’s oratory wednesdays 7.30 - 8.30pm reflection before jesus present in the blessed sacrament . newsletter articles for the newsletter must be received by 12 noon on thursdays. parish office opening hours monday 2nd november – 9.30am to 1pm. please note the parish office is closed tuesday 3rd november & will re-open on monday 9th november. anniversaries etc. can be left in the sacristy before mass during this time o r left into the parish centre post box up until 12 noon on thursday. baltinglass

. the irish cancer society is seeking compassionate volunteer drivers to join our pool of drivers. as a volunteer driver you would be bringing patients undergoing chemotherapy to the hospital and back home for their treatment. gifting your time means that cancer patients will have comfortable (one on one) transport to attend appointments for their lifesaving treatment. if you can spare 2 days per month, have a valid driving licence, and a safe, reliable vehicle, you are the perfect candidate to make a significant difference. the irish cancer society will provide you with training before you start as a driver for us. your generosity not only eases the journey for many during a challenging time but also offers comfort and support when it's needed most. to become a volunteer driver, email monica or emily at
